Kir Leshkevich

Hi Product Hunt! I'm Kir, and I've been building desigma: a free, open-source design tool that runs natively on Windows, macOS and Linux.

I wanted a design tool I actually own. No account, no seats, no subscription, files on my own disk, and source code I can read and change. So desigma is written in pure Rust, with its own renderer, and it works offline.

What's in it today:

• Frames, auto layout, components with variants and properties, variables with modes

• Prototyping with Smart Animate, plus a Motion timeline with keyframes, springs and 41 presets (export to GIF/WebM)

• Whiteboards (stickies, connectors, timer and voting) and slide decks, in the same app [...] • Dev mode with CSS, Tailwind, React, SwiftUI and Compose, and an MCP server so AI agents can edit the open file

• It opens .fig files and REST JSON exports

New this week: live collaboration. Click Share, send the link, and everyone edits the same file in real time with cursors and Follow. It's peer-to-peer and encrypted, so there's still no account and no server. If you want a file online all the time, you can run desigma-server on a VPS.

It's an early alpha, so expect rough edges. Builds aren't code-signed yet, so your OS will warn you on first launch (the install guide explains the one click).

I'd love to hear what you'd need to switch for a real project, and what breaks. I'll be here all day answering.

Figma is fantastic because it enables real-time collaboration and design iteration in a way that fundamentally changes how teams work together. Its browser-based architecture removes setup friction, while features like live co-editing, shared components, and design systems allow designers, developers, and product teams to stay aligned at all times. By unifying design, prototyping, and feedback into a single platform, Figma significantly improves speed, clarity, and cross-functional collaboration.
